Specify an MRQAP from a formula written for any model

Source: R/specify_formula.R, R/specify_report.R
specify_mrqap.Rd

specify_mrqap() reads a formula, whichever model it was written for, and returns the formula that estimate_mrqap() fits from it. estimate_mrqap() calls it on every formula. specify_ergm() reads the same formulas for ergm::ergm(), specify_saom() for RSiena::siena(), and {goldfish}'s own specify_dynam() for a DyNAM or REM.

A term with an equivalent in the model is rewritten as that term. A term that means something different in the model is kept and named. A term the model cannot fit is dropped and named, so that the rest of the model still fits. Rewritten and differently interpreted terms are reported with manynet::snet_info(), which is silent unless options(snet_verbosity = "verbose"), and dropped terms are reported in one warning. A formula aborts only where no term is left to fit. A name that no model knows is left for the fitting function, which then aborts and suggests the nearest name.

Usage

specify_mrqap(formula, .data = NULL, input = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_formula'
summary(object, .data = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_formula'
tidy(x, .data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

formula

A formula written for an MRQAP, goldfish, ergm, or RSiena, or a sienaEffects object. Without it, or with . as its right-hand side, the table of every term for .data, as specify_terms describes.

.data

Optionally, the network the formula is for. With it, a bare name that is a layer of the network stays a layer. In summary(), the network to build the columns from.

input

The model the formula was written for: "mrqap", "dynam", "rem", "ergm", or "saom". NULL, the default, reads it from the class of the formula, such as goldfish's "goldfishFormula", or else from the names in the formula.

object, x

A formula returned by specify_mrqap().

...

Not used.

Value

A formula of class c("mrqap_formula", "formula"). Its input attribute names the model it was read from, and its record attribute holds what the model makes of each term. Printing the formula lists the terms that do not fit as written and returns the formula, invisibly. summary() returns every term as a tibble, with the columns term, status, as, reason, and columns. tidy() of a specification is deprecated: it gives the same table and warns once. Without a formula, the table of every term for .data, as specify_terms describes.

What each model makes of each term

summary() of the result has one row for each term of the formula, and fits nothing. Its status is what the model makes of the term:

  • "fits": the model fits the term as it is written;

  • "adapted": the term is rewritten as its equivalent in the model, in as;

  • "interpreted": the model has a term of the same name that it defines differently, as reason says;

  • "warns": the model fits the term, but with a warning, as reason says;

  • "drops": the model cannot fit the term, so it is left out, and the rest is fitted;

  • "refuses": the model aborts, as reason says.

An MRQAP warns for a term that reads the outcome's own ties, such as recip, and refuses tie(), indeg(), and outdeg() of the outcome layer. It drops an offset, such as goldfish's offset(recip, coef = 0), since it estimates every coefficient; ergm keeps an ergm one. For an MRQAP, summary() with .data also builds each term and names its columns, as estimate_mrqap() names them.

Reading the model a formula was written for

The model a formula was written for is read, in order, from input, from the class of the formula, such as "ergm_formula", or from the names in the formula:

  • "ergm" where a term is named only in ergm, such as edges, mutual, or nodematch("x");

  • "saom" where an effect is named only in RSiena, such as transTrip, inPop, or egoX(sex);

  • "dynam" where a term is named only in goldfish, such as inertia or trans;

  • "mrqap" otherwise.

A sienaEffects object of {RSiena} is read as the formula of the evaluation effects it includes for its first dependent network.

The model that was read is reported. Where a formula mixes ergm's names with goldfish's, it is read as an ergm formula, and goldfish's names in it are read as they are in goldfish. The result of each function carries its model as its class, so that specify_ergm(specify_mrqap(f)) reads its input without a guess.

ergm and infernet

ergm names an attribute with a string, and infernet with a bare name. Both read levels = as names or positions. infernet does not read ergm's functions for levels =, such as LARGEST, or nodemix()'s levels =, which changes the positions of levels2 =: such a term is left to ergm, and an MRQAP drops it. terms_mrqap gives each term's ergm equivalent.

Read from ergm, nodecov("x") becomes ego(x) + alter(x), and edges and density are the intercept, which an MRQAP always has. ergm's terms of the outcome's own structure, such as gwesp(), and its node fixed effects, sender, receiver, and sociality, are kept for ergm and dropped for an MRQAP, where (1 | sender) adds a random intercept instead. The left-hand side of an ergm formula names the network rather than a layer, so where it names no layer or tie attribute of .data, the outcome is read as ..

goldfish and infernet

goldfish's terms are infernet's where the two packages share them, as terms_mrqap lists. sim() is 1 - |d| / range in infernet and -|d| in goldfish, which changes the scale of its coefficient but not its test, and tertius() and tertius_diff() leave out the sender in infernet and include it in goldfish. Both are kept and named.

For an MRQAP, goldfish's endogenous effects, such as cycle, common_sender, common_receiver, and four, read the outcome's own ties, which permuting the outcome would not permute with them, so they are dropped. So are goldfish's closures through two layers and the DyNAM-i statistics of groups. inertia, recip, and trans read the outcome's previous wave where .data is a longitudinal network, and fit there; on a cross-sectional network, inertia and trans are dropped too.

goldfish names the side of indeg() and outdeg() with type =, and reads the receiver for both by default, where infernet's outdeg() reads the sender. A goldfish formula is read as goldfish reads it: outdeg(friends) becomes outdeg(friends, node = "alter"), with a warning, and type = becomes node =. indeg or outdeg on its own reads the outcome's own degree in goldfish, and is dropped for an MRQAP and for ergm. goldfish's older formulas name a node attribute with its table of nodes, as in ego(actors$floor), which is read as ego(floor), since the network holds its nodes' attributes.

See also

terms_mrqap for what each term measures, and specify_terms for the terms that suit a network.

Other specifying functions: declare_coefs(), declare_coefs_ergm, specify_ergm(), specify_saom(), specify_terms, terms_mrqap

Examples

# An ergm formula, read for an MRQAP
specify_mrqap(advice ~ edges + mutual + nodematch("dept") + edgecov("friends"))
#> # An MRQAP formula read from a formula for ergm
#> 
#> advice ~ recip + same(dept) + friends
#> 
#> # adapted edges: is the intercept that the model always has
#> # adapted mutual -> recip
#> # adapted nodematch("dept") -> same(dept)
#> # adapted edgecov("friends") -> friends
# A goldfish formula, read for an MRQAP
f <- suppressWarnings(
  specify_mrqap(advice ~ inertia + recip + trans + ego(age)))
f
#> # An MRQAP formula read from a formula for goldfish
#> 
#> advice ~ recip + ego(age)
#> 
#> # drops inertia: needs a longitudinal network, where it reads the outcome's
#> #   previous wave
#> # warns recip: reads the outcome's own ties, which permuting the outcome does
#> #   not permute with it
#> # drops trans: needs a longitudinal network, where it reads the outcome's
#> #   previous wave
# Each term, and what the model makes of it
summary(f)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   term     status as       reason                                        columns
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>    <chr>                                         <list> 
#> 1 inertia  drops  NA       needs a longitudinal network, where it reads… <chr>  
#> 2 recip    warns  recip    reads the outcome's own ties, which permutin… <chr>  
#> 3 trans    drops  NA       needs a longitudinal network, where it reads… <chr>  
#> 4 ego(age) fits   ego(age) NA                                            <chr>  
g <- specify_mrqap(advice ~ ego(age) + same(dept) + recip(friends), ison_hightech)
summary(g, ison_hightech)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   term           status as             reason columns  
#>   <chr>          <chr>  <chr>          <chr>  <list>   
#> 1 ego(age)       fits   ego(age)       NA     <chr [1]>
#> 2 same(dept)     fits   same(dept)     NA     <chr [1]>
#> 3 recip(friends) fits   recip(friends) NA     <chr [1]>
